flashcards.q: Is a VNet regional or global, and how does this differ from GCP?
flashcards.a: VNets are regional, same as AWS VPCs. GCP VPCs are global with per-region subnets under one VPC object -- multi-region connectivity in GCP needs no peering, unlike Azure/AWS.

flashcards.q: What is the structural difference between an NSG and an ASG?
flashcards.a: NSG is the actual filter: a prioritized allow/deny rule list matched on IP/port/protocol, attached to a subnet and/or NIC. ASG is not a filter -- it's a group label assigned to NICs that an NSG rule can reference as source/destination instead of a hardcoded IP.

flashcards.q: State the hard NSG rule ceiling and the standard mitigation.
flashcards.a: 2,000 rules per NSG (custom + default combined), not raisable. Mitigation: augmented security rules (multiple IP ranges/ports collapsed into one rule) or ASG-based grouping instead of individual IP-based rules.

flashcards.q: State VNet peering's key limits and its transitivity behavior.
flashcards.a: 500 peering connections per VNet by default (extensible to 1,000 via Azure Virtual Network Manager), 200 subnets per side of one peering link, 1,000 total subnets per VNet across all peerings. Peering is explicitly NON-TRANSITIVE.

flashcards.q: Is Application Gateway regional or global, and what is its pricing model?
flashcards.a: Regional, VNet-scoped L7 load balancer with integrated WAF v2. Pricing: fixed ~$0.443/gateway-hour plus variable ~$0.0144/capacity-unit-hour.

flashcards.q: Compare Front Door Standard and Premium tiers.
flashcards.a: Standard (~$35/month base) includes only custom WAF rules. Premium (~$330/month base) adds the managed OWASP WAF rule set and Private Link origin support (reaching a backend with zero public IP).

flashcards.q: Why aren't Application Gateway and Front Door interchangeable?
flashcards.a: Application Gateway is regional and VNet-scoped -- no cross-region failover awareness. Front Door is a global anycast edge service with health-probe-driven cross-region failover. A common production pattern layers Front Door Premium at the edge in front of per-region Application Gateways.

flashcards.q: What is the most common Private Link deployment failure?
flashcards.a: Creating a Private Endpoint without linking a Private DNS Zone to the VNet -- clients still resolve the PaaS resource's public FQDN and hit the public endpoint instead of the private one, leaving the private endpoint effectively unused.

flashcards.q: Does creating a Private Endpoint automatically disable a resource's public network access?
flashcards.a: No. Public network access is a separate setting on the resource itself. A Private Endpoint adds a private path without removing the public one unless public access is explicitly disabled after confirming all clients have private connectivity.

flashcards.q: State the key Private Link scale limits.
flashcards.a: 1,000 private endpoints per virtual network; 400 Key Vaults with private endpoints per subscription; up to 8 NAT IP addresses per Private Link Service.

flashcards.q: How many ASGs can a single NSG rule reference as source or destination?
flashcards.a: Up to 10 ASGs as source and 10 as destination in a single NSG rule.

flashcards.q: Map Azure's networking stack to its AWS equivalents.
flashcards.a: VNet~=VPC. NSG+ASG~=Security Group (self-referencing), Azure splits filter from label into two objects. Application Gateway~=ALB+AWS WAF. Front Door~=CloudFront+AWS WAF+Global Accelerator combined into one product. Private Link~=AWS PrivateLink/VPC endpoint.
